raw_response:
I am 65 years old, and I have farmed this land since I was 25. I only finished primary school, but I know my field. My piece is only 1.5 mu, so every jiao I spend matters. My son works in a factory in Handan and sends some money home, but I still calculate carefully — a bag of fertilizer is 150 yuan, and that is real money.

Last year I planted Denghai 605, the hybrid seed. Before that I used some local variety, but Old Wang next door used Denghai 605 and his maize was taller and the ears were fatter than mine. So I switched, and my yield got better. This year I will buy Denghai 605 again from the seed dealer in town. It costs more, but I saw it work with my own eyes on Wang's field, so I trust it.

For fertilizer, I do what I did last year. I buy three 50-jin bags of compound fertilizer from the dealer — the red bag that says it is for maize, 25% nitrogen. Three bags for my 1.5 mu means one bag for every half-mu. I spread one and a half bags when I plant in late April, and the other one and a half bags I put down when the maize is knee-high, around mid-June. I know three bags costs nearly 450 yuan, but if I use less, the ears will be small and I will lose more than I saved. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost. I do not buy extra urea — the compound is enough if I put it down twice.

I have a well right next to the field, so I irrigate three times. First, right after planting. Second, when the maize is jointing, around mid-June. Third, when the ears are filling grain in August. If it rains hard I might skip one, but three times is what I always do.

For pests, I spray herbicide once after planting to kill the weeds. Then I spray insecticide twice — once when the seedlings are small, and again in August when the corn borers come. That is three sprays total. I do it myself with the backpack sprayer. I do not hire labor — my daughter-in-law helps when she is not at her job.

I rotary till the soil in mid-April before planting. My nephew has a small rotary tiller, and he does it for me for 50 yuan. I do not plough deep — rotary is enough, and the dealer told me it keeps the moisture in the ground better.

I expect my 1.5 mu to give me about 1500 jin of maize this year. That is about 1000 jin per mu. Last year I got a little less because July was too dry, but this year I think it will be normal.
